Applying this approach revealed that gut bacteria sulfonate hydroxy fatty acids, leading to the identification of the commensal bacterium Eubacterium ramulus and its functional sulfotransferase ErSULT.
key_finding_ja: ヒト腸内細菌Eubacterium ramulusが酵素ErSULTを介してヒドロキシ脂肪酸を硫酸化することを明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内微生物が生成する硫酸化小分子とその合成酵素の同定は、微生物由来代謝物が宿主の代謝や免疫系に与える影響の解明を促す可能性がある。

title: Aurantio-Obtusin Attenuates Aβ-Induced Cognitive Impairment and Synaptic Dysfunction by Suppressing Neuroinflammation in Mice.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) features Aβ-driven neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction that converge on cognitive decline, underscoring the potential value of multi-target interventions. Aurantio-obtusin (AO), a bioactive anthraquinone from Cassia obtusifolia L., exhibits reported anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities; however, whether AO counteracts Aβ-associated behavioral impairment through coordinated modulation of inflammatory and synaptic alterations remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether AO alleviates Aβ₁₋₄₂-induced cognitive deficits and examined synapse- and inflammation-related molecular correlates. Male C57BL/6 mice received intracerebroventricular Aβ₁₋₄₂ to establish an acute AD-like model and were treated with AO (10 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) for consecutive weeks. The results showed that AO improved spatial learning and memory in the Morris water maze, recognition memory in the novel object recognition test, and working memory in the Y-maze, without affecting spontaneous locomotor activity. Furthermore, AO alleviated synaptic dysfunction by restoring synaptophysin expression and upregulating GAD65, and mitigated neuroinflammation by elevating anti-inflammatory factors (IL-4, IL-10, ARG1) and reducing TNF-α. In vitro experiments confirmed that AO was non-cytotoxic to N2A APP cells across 0-80 μM, mildly downregulated BACE1 expression, and suppressed the Aβ-induced upregulation of pro-inflammatory mediators (IL-6, iNOS) in BV2 microglial cells. Overall, AO attenuated Aβ 1-42 -driven behavioral impairment in parallel with improvements in synapse-associated markers and inflammatory readouts. These findings support further evaluation of AO as a natural compound associated with modulation of Aβ-related neuroinflammatory and synapse-associated alterations.
authors: Feng X, Yu W, Guo S, Ji Y, Li J, Wang L, Zhong G, Li S, Niu L, Zhu D, Zhou K, Du Y.
journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
screening_reason: The principal finding demonstrates that Aurantio-Obtusin attenuates cognitive impairment by directly suppressing neuroinflammation and microglial inflammatory mediators.
summary_ja: エビスグサ種子由来の化合物オウランティオオプチシン（AO）が、アミロイドベータ（Aβ1-42）誘発性の認知機能障害および神経炎症に与える影響をマウスモデルで検証した。AOの投与により、水迷路試験や新規物体認知試験における学習・記憶障害が改善し、自発運動量に影響を与えることなく作業記憶も回復した。さらにAOはシナプトフィジンの発現回復や抗炎症性因子の増加、TNF-αの低下をもたらした。インビトロ実験においても、AOはミクログリアにおける炎症性メディエーターの発現を抑制することが確認された。
summary_en: This study evaluated the protective effects of aurantio-obtusin (AO) against Aβ1-42-induced cognitive deficits and neuroinflammation in a mouse model. Treatment with AO restored spatial and working memory while improving synapse-associated markers and increasing anti-inflammatory cytokines. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that AO suppressed Aβ-induced pro-inflammatory mediators in microglial cells.
key_finding_ja: オウランティオオプチシンは、Aβ投与マウスにおいて神経炎症を抑えシナプス機能を回復させることで認知機能障害を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: アミロイドベータによる神経炎症とシナプス機能障害を同時に標的とする天然化合物の新たな治療候補として期待されるが、今後の詳細な作用機序解明が求められる。

title: Citrullination and Deamidation in Type 1 Diabetes: Linking Beta Cell Stress to Neoantigen-Driven Autoimmunity.
abstract: Citrullination and deamidation are post-translational modifications (PTMs) increasingly recognized as important contributors to neoepitope formation in type 1 diabetes (T1D). Under inflammatory and endoplasmic reticulum stress conditions, beta cells activate calcium-dependent peptidylarginine deiminase and transglutaminase enzymes, leading to self-protein modification, altered peptide charge and HLA-binding properties, thereby generating neoepitopes that can be recognized by autoreactive CD4 + and CD8 + T cells. Accumulating evidence from both murine and human studies demonstrates that immune responses against citrullinated and deamidated beta cell proteins are present and increase with disease progression, supporting a role in epitope spreading rather than disease initiation. Although both PTMs are biochemically analogous, their kinetics and regulation are distinct: citrullination appears as an earlier and partly intrinsic response of stressed beta cells, whereas deamidation is more closely associated with sustained inflammation and later disease stages. In parallel, reduced PTM-generating enzyme expression in the thymus may limit central tolerance to modified epitopes, facilitating escape of autoreactive T cells. In this review, we summarize current insights into the biochemical and immunological roles of citrullination and deamidation in T1D, with emphasis on their temporal regulation, contribution to neoepitope formation, and potential as therapeutic targets, highlighting key findings from our own work in the field.
authors: Callebaut A, Bruggeman Y, Mathieu C, James EA, Overbergh L.
screening_reason: The paper focuses directly on protein post-translational modifications (citrullination and deamidation) and their mechanistic role in generating neoepitopes.
summary_ja: 本総説は、1型糖尿病（T1D）におけるタンパク質翻訳後修飾（シトルリン化および脱アミド化）とネオ抗原形成のメカニズムを解説している。炎症や小胞体ストレス下で活性化した酵素により自己タンパク質が修飾され、抗原提示分子への結合性が変化することで自動活性化T細胞が認識するネオエピトープが生じる。シトルリン化はストレスを受けた膵β細胞の初期応答として生じるのに対し、脱アミド化は持続的な炎症や病期の進行とより強く関連している。また、胸腺における修飾酵素の発現低下が中枢性寛容の回避を促進する可能性が指摘されている。
summary_en: This review outlines the roles of post-translational modifications, specifically citrullination and deamidation, in generating neoepitopes during type 1 diabetes progression. Beta cell stress activates modifying enzymes that alter self-proteins, resulting in neoepitopes recognized by autoreactive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. While citrullination represents an early stress response, deamidation correlates with sustained inflammation in later disease stages.
key_finding_ja: シトルリン化と脱アミド化は異なる時間的制御を受けて膵β細胞のネオ抗原を形成し、1型糖尿病における自己免疫反応の拡大に貢献している。
why_it_matters_ja: 翻訳後修飾に由来するネオ抗原の生成機序を解明することは、1型糖尿病の早期診断マーカーや特異的免疫療法の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: β-hydroxybutyrate regulates microglia M1/M2 polarization and phagocytosis through the JAK1/STAT1 pathway to reduce neuroinflammation and exert anti-epileptic effects.
abstract: Neuroinflammation and microglia M1/M2 polarization imbalance are among the core pathological mechanisms of epilepsy (EP), with the JAK1/STAT1 pathway being vital in neuroinflammation. β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), a ketone body metabolite, has anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective potential, but whether it can ameliorate EP-related neurological damage by modulating this pathway remains unclear. To investigate whether BHB regulates microglia polarization and phagocytosis through the JAK1/STAT1 pathway, attenuates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury, and thus exerts anti-EP effects. A rat primary neuronal EP model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced M1-type microglia model were constructed, and microglia polarization, migration, phagocytosis, and neuronal damage were detected by scratch assay, flow cytometry, Hoechst 33,342/PI staining, Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, and ELISA kits. A rat model of Pentetrazol (PTZ)-induced EP was constructed to detect the effects of BHB on the symptoms of EP in rats by behavioral assessment, and to detect brain tissue damage by pathological staining. Western blot was conducted to detect microglia polarization markers, neuronal apoptosis, synapse-related proteins, and JAK1/STAT1 pathway-related proteins expression. Pathway specificity was verified using JAK1 overexpression plasmid (OE-JAK1) and STAT1 inhibitor (Fludarabine). BHB concentration-dependently increased EP neuron viability and suppressed M1 polarization induced by LPS, and promoted M2 polarization. BHB also enhanced the migration and phagocytosis of microglia, and reduced pro-inflammatory factor release, which in turn attenuated their pro-inflammatory damage to neurons and protected synaptic integrity, and this effect was linked to its suppression of JAK1/STAT1 pathway activation. Additionally, BHB extended seizure latency, decreased seizure duration, and reduced seizure severity in EP rats, and effectively attenuated brain histopathological damage and promoted neuronal regeneration and axonal repair. Furthermore, BHB was also effective in promoting microglia M2 polarization and enhancing their phagocytosis in vivo. Overexpression of JAK1 attenuated the neuroprotective effects of BHB, and Fludarabine attenuated the impacts of overexpression of JAK1. By inhibiting the JAK1/STAT1 pathway, BHB promotes microglia M2 polarization and enhances their phagocytosis, attenuates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury, and ultimately exerts anti-EP effects.
authors: Yang H, Wang H.
screening_reason: Demonstrates that beta-hydroxybutyrate regulates microglial polarization and phagocytosis via JAK1/STAT1 signaling to suppress neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: てんかんにおける神経炎症とミクログリアのM1/M2分極異常に対するβ-ヒドロキシ酪酸（BHB）の作用機序をラットモデルおよび細胞モデルで解析した。BHBはJAK1/STAT1経路の活性化を抑制することで、LPS誘発性M1分極を抑え、M2分極と貪食能を促進した。さらに、PTZ誘発てんかんラットにおいてBHBは発作潜時の延長や重症度の低下をもたらし、脳組織損傷を軽減した。JAK1の過剰発現はBHBの保護効果を減弱させ、STAT1阻害剤はこの過剰発現の影響を打ち消した。
summary_en: This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) in rat epilepsy models and microglial cell cultures. BHB promoted microglial M2 polarization, enhanced phagocytosis, and suppressed neuroinflammation by inhibiting the JAK1/STAT1 pathway. In vivo, BHB reduced seizure severity and brain histopathological damage, which was attenuated by JAK1 overexpression.
key_finding_ja: β-ヒドロキシ酪酸はJAK1/STAT1経路を抑制することでミクログリアのM2極性化と貪食能を促進し、神経炎症およびてんかん症状を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: BHBによるミクログリア極性化の制御機構の解明は、てんかんにおける神経炎症を標的とした新たな治療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: The emerging role of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology.
abstract: Purpose of review Purpose of the review is provision of an up-to-date literature review on the growing importance of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology and its limitations. Recent findings Traditionally, the diagnostic role of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology lies in the initial suspicion of motility disorders and exclusion of important differential diagnoses. Endoscopy may serve also as a carrier for positioning examination devices such as the Bravo reflux-capsule to proof gastroesophageal reflux or the endoluminal functional lumen imaging probe (EndoFLIP). New interesting aspects are the resection-based and biopsy-based extraction of tissue for examination of the enteric nervous system by the full thickness resection device (FTRD) to detect structural gastrointestinal neuromuscular lesion and confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) to investigate potential correlations for food intolerance. Effectiveness of endoscopic therapy is dependent on whether the measured circumscribed dysfunction correlates with the symptoms and explains them. This is the case in esophageal achalasia and hypercontractile motility disorders. However, in gastropareses, the significance of endoscopic therapy is limited because of its complex pathophysiology. Summary There is an emerging role of endoscopy in neurogastroenetrology. However, effectiveness of endoscopic therapy is dependent on careful patient selection and evidence of a circumscribed dysfunction that correlates with the symptoms and explains them.
authors: Frieling T.
screening_reason: Discusses endoscopic techniques for tissue extraction and examination of the enteric nervous system and GI motility in neurogastroenterology.
summary_ja: 神経消化器病学における内視鏡検査の新たな役割とその限界について文献レビューが行われた。内視鏡はアカラシア等の運動障害の診断補助やBravoカプセル、EndoFLIPなどの検査機器の留置に用いられている。さらに、全層生検による腸管神経系の評価や、共焦点レーザー内視鏡を用いた食物不耐症の検討も進んでいる。内視鏡治療の有効性は、症状に対応する局所的な機能障害の証明と適切な患者選択に依存することが示されている。
summary_en: This review outlines the evolving role and limitations of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology. Endoscopic methods facilitate the placement of diagnostic devices, tissue extraction for enteric nervous system evaluation, and targeted therapeutic interventions. The clinical effectiveness of endoscopic therapy depends heavily on precise patient selection and demonstrated focal dysfunction correlating with symptoms.
key_finding_ja: 内視鏡検査は運動障害の診断機器留置や腸管神経系の組織採取、局所的障害に対する治療において新たな役割を果たしている。
why_it_matters_ja: 内視鏡技術の発展は消化管運動障害の正確な診断や適切な治療対象患者の選別に寄与する可能性が生じている。

title: Multipathway modulation of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress by hesperidin in a rat single prolonged stress model of post-traumatic stress disorder.
abstract: Background Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complicated neuropsychiatric disorder that is marked by long-term neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and poor neuroplasticity in stress-sensitive brain areas. Hesperidin is a citrus-derived flavanone glycoside that has been reported to have multitarget neuroprotective effects with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic regulatory activities. However, its integrated effects across convergent pathological pathways in validated PTSD models remain insufficiently defined. Methods Male Wistar rats were subjected to the single prolonged stress (SPS) paradigm and treated with hesperidin (50, 100, and 200 mg/kg), fluoxetine (20 mg/kg), or vehicle for 14 days. Biochemical assessments (malondialdehyde [MDA], catalase [CAT], superoxide dismutase [SOD]) and immunohistochemical measurements of neuronal and glial integrity (NeuN, glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP], brain-derived neurotrophic factor [BDNF]) in the hippocampus, amygdala, and prefrontal cortex were performed. Results SPS exposure induced marked oxidative imbalance, evidenced by increased MDA levels and reduced CAT activity, alongside significant upregulation of tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and IL-1β, increased astrocytic reactivity (GFAP), and reduced BDNF expression. Hesperidin treatment significantly attenuated lipid peroxidation, partially restored CAT activity, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines, with the most pronounced effect observed for IL-1β. Notably, hesperidin reduced astrocytic activation and preserved neuronal morphology, while enhancing BDNF expression in a dose-dependent manner, with optimal effects at 50-100 mg/kg. Conversely, there was little group variation in the activity of SOD, implying pathway-selective redox regulation. Conclusion Hesperidin has multipathway, coordinated, modulatory effects on oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, glial activation, and neurotrophic signaling in the SPS model of PTSD. These findings support its utility as a mechanistic probe for interrogating convergent stress-related neuropathological pathways.
authors: Anyanwu GE, Akanaku OC, Oviosun A, Ekwueme PE, Odey PA, Okechukwu Ugwu CP, Anyanwu CN.
screening_reason: Studies the attenuation of neuroinflammation, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and glial reactivity by hesperidin in a PTSD model.
summary_ja: PTSDの単一長時間ストレス（SPS）ラットモデルを用い、ヘスペリジンの神経保護効果と多角的な作用機序を検証した。SPS曝露は酸化ストレスの上昇、炎症性サイトカイン（TNF-α、IL-6、IL-1β）の増加、アストロサイト活性化（GFAP増強）、ならびにBDNF発現の低下を引き起こした。ヘスペリジン投与により、脂質過酸化の抑制、炎症性サイトカインの減少、アストロサイトの活性化抑制、BDNF発現の上昇および神経細胞形態の保持が確認された。
summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of hesperidin in a rat single prolonged stress (SPS) model of post-traumatic stress disorder. SPS exposure induced oxidative stress, pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, astrocytic activation, and reduced BDNF levels across stress-sensitive brain regions. Treatment with hesperidin reduced lipid peroxidation, suppressed inflammatory cytokines, attenuated astrocytic reactivity, and restored BDNF expression in a dose-dependent manner.
key_finding_ja: ヘスペリジンはSPS誘導PTSDモデルにおいて、酸化ストレス、神経炎症、アストロサイトの活性化、ならびにBDNF低下を多角的に改善する。
why_it_matters_ja: ストレス関連精神疾患における病理メカニズムの解明や、新規治療法開発のための薬理学的ツールとしてヘスペリジンの有用性が期待される。

title: From dysbiotic gut to malodorous mouth: targeting microbial metabolism for gastrointestinal type halitosis.
abstract: This article reviews the microbiological mechanisms of halitosis, the oral-gut axis, the role of the gut microbiome, related metabolic pathways, and their associations with gastrointestinal diseases, and explores intervention strategies based on microbial regulation. Halitosis is primarily caused by volatile sulfur compounds produced by oral microorganisms, especially gram-negative anaerobic bacteria, and volatile organic compounds in most extraoral etiologies. Studies have found that intestinal microbial dysregulation can affect the composition of oral flora through the oral-gut axis and aggravate bad breath. Gastrointestinal diseases, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease, Helicobacter pylori infection, ulcerative colitis and irritable bowel syndrome can directly or indirectly promote the occurrence of bad breath by changing the intestinal microenvironment and microbial metabolic pathways, such as protein spoilage or short-chain fatty acids imbalance, etc. For microbial interventions, traditional Chinese medicine can not only systemically regulate the oral-gut axis balance, but also effectively alleviate bad breath by targeting sterilization and inhibiting the metabolic activity of pathogenic bacteria. This review focuses on elucidating the complex links between halitosis and the gut microbiome, its metabolic pathways, and gastrointestinal diseases, emphasizing the key role of microbial metabolites in pathological mechanisms. It reveals the importance of the oral-gut axis in systemic health and provides a rationale for developing personalized halitosis management strategies based on microbiome regulation.
authors: Liang X, Deng Y, Zhao L, Zhou X, Li Z, Xiao G, Chen S.
screening_reason: The review focuses on the gut microbiome, microbial metabolism, and the gut-oral axis in gastrointestinal conditions.
summary_ja: 本論文は、口臭（口臭症）と腸内細菌叢、微生物代謝産物、および消化器疾患との関連について論じた総説である。腸内細菌叢の乱れは口腔-腸軸を通じて口腔内菌叢の構成や短鎖脂肪酸等の代謝バランスを変化させ、口臭を増悪させることが知られている。逆流性食道炎やヘリコバクター・ピロリ感染症などの胃腸疾患は、腸内環境を変化させることで口臭発生に寄与する。本総説では微生物代謝の観点から口臭の病態を整理し、漢方薬など微生物調節を標的とした介入の可能性を議論している。
summary_en: This review highlights the interplay between the gut microbiome, microbial metabolic pathways, and halitosis via the oral-gut axis. Dysbiosis and gastrointestinal disorders alter microbial metabolites such as volatile sulfur compounds and short-chain fatty acids, contributing to bad breath. The authors discuss potential microbiome-targeted interventions, including traditional Chinese medicine, for managing gastrointestinal-associated halitosis.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢の乱れと代謝産物の変動が口腔-腸軸を介して口臭や消化器疾患の病態に関与していることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 微生物代謝や口腔-腸軸を標的とした個別化アプローチは、口臭および関連する消化器不調の管理に新たな選択肢をもたらす可能性がある。

title: Exercise-Mediated Modulation of the NLRP3 Inflammasome in Aging and Neurodegenerative Diseases: Mechanisms, Microglial Crosstalk, and Translational Perspectives.
abstract: Regular engagement in physical exercise has been recognized as a formidable non-pharmacological intervention aimed at mitigating age-associated neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative phenomena. A fundamental mechanism that underpins these advantageous effects pertains to the modulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, which serves as a pivotal regulator of innate immune responses within microglial cells. The aging process is marked by a state of chronic low-grade inflammation, commonly referred to as "inflammaging," which is instigated by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and metabolic disturbances; these factors collectively facilitate the activation of NLRP3 and the subsequent secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines, notably IL-1β. Contemporary research findings suggest that physical exercise diminishes NLRP3 inflammasome activation through various interrelated pathways. These pathways encompass the reduction of reactive oxygen species production, the inhibition of TXNIP-mediated assembly of the inflammasome, and the modulation of metabolites derived from the gut, such as trimethylamine N-oxide. In addition, factors circulating as a result of exercise, which include irisin and meteorin-like protein, play a significant role in promoting systemic and central anti-inflammatory responses, thereby impacting the functional dynamics of microglia. In experimental paradigms investigating the phenomena of aging and neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), notably Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, physical activity has been shown to diminish amyloid accumulation, tau pathology, and microglial activation, primarily through the attenuation of NLRP3 signaling pathways. Collectively, these observations underscore the role of exercise as a pivotal regulator of neuroimmune equilibrium, thereby providing mechanistic elucidation of its potential therapeutic efficacy in alleviating inflammaging and decelerating the progression of NDDs.
authors: Zhang Y.
screening_reason: The review centers on exercise-induced regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, microglial activation, and neuroimmune equilibrium in neurodegenerative diseases.
summary_ja: 本論文は、加齢や神経変性疾患における有酸素運動・身体活動によるNLRP3インフラマソームの調節機構について概説した総説である。加齢に伴う慢性的な微小炎症（インフラメイジング）では、ミクログリアのNLRP3インフラマソームが活性化されプロ炎症性サイトカインが分泌される。運動は活性酸素種の減少や循環因子、腸内細菌由来代謝産物の修飾を介してNLRP3の活性化を抑制し、ミクログリアの活性化を軽減する。実験モデルでは、運動がアミロイド蓄積やタウ病理を抑制し、神経免疫の平衡維持に寄与することが示されている。
summary_en: This review highlights how physical exercise regulates the NLRP3 inflammasome in microglia to suppress age-related neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative pathology. Exercise reduces ROS production, influences circulating factors and gut-derived metabolites, and attenuates amyloid and tau pathology in experimental models. These findings emphasize physical activity as a key non-pharmacological modulator of neuroimmune equilibrium.
key_finding_ja: 運動はNLRP3インフラマソームの活性化を抑制することでミクログリアの炎症応答を減弱させ、神経変性疾患の病理変化を軽減する。
why_it_matters_ja: 運動によるミクログリア活性化抑制の分子メカニズム解明は、加齢性神経変性疾患に対する非薬物療法の理論的基盤を強化する可能性がある。

title: Cross-link Between CircRNAs and Neuroinflammation in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a major neurodegenerative disorder affecting a large number of people worldwide. PD has been characterized by motor abnormalities, as well as non-motor abnormalities that lower patients' quality of life. The pathological features of PD include the substantia nigra's dopaminergic neurons degradation, leading to a progressive clinical course, Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites, which are primarily composed of α-synuclein, and chronic neuroinflammatory changes that contribute to disease progression. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are a type of circular single-stranded RNAs possessing high stability. Their expression varies depending on tissue type, cell type, and developmental stage, suggesting their roles in regulating biological processes. Recent research has indicated that circRNAs participate in PD pathophysiology by modulating neuroinflammation, immune response, mitochondrial dysfunction, and reactive oxygen species accumulation. Mechanistically, many circRNAs appear to act as molecular sponges for microRNAs, thereby influencing the expression of key genes involved in inflammatory signaling, synaptic regulation, and neuronal survival. This review summarizes the impact of circRNAs on neuroinflammation, astrocyte/microglia dysfunction, mitochondrial damage, and oxidative stress in PD. It also summarizes experimental evidence from cellular and animal models showing that multiple circRNAs can modulate inflammatory pathways in PD and related neurological disorders. However, only a limited number of studies have evaluated circRNAs as biomarkers or therapeutic targets in patient samples, and comprehensive in vivo validation of circRNA-miRNA-target network remains insufficient. A better understanding of these regulatory pathways may help identify clinically relevant biomarkers and support the development of circRNA-based therapeutic strategies for PD.
authors: El-Ashmawy NE, Khedr EG, Darwish RT, Ibrahim AO.
screening_reason: The review focuses on the central role of circRNAs in modulating neuroinflammation and microglial/astrocytic activation in Parkinson's disease.
summary_ja: 本論文は、パーキンソン病（PD）の病態生理における環状RNA（circRNA）と神経炎症の相互作用についてまとめた総説である。circRNAは高安定な環状単一鎖RNAであり、microRNAの分子スポンジとして機能することで炎症シグナル伝達や神経細胞の生存に関わる遺伝子発現を調節する。細胞モデルや動物モデルの研究から、複数のcircRNAがミクログリアやアストロサイトの機能異常、ミトコンドリア障害、酸化ストレスを制御することが示されている。しかし、患者検体におけるバイオマーカーや治療標的としての検証、ならびに生体内での調節ネットワークの網羅的解析はまだ不十分である。
summary_en: This review discusses the role of circular RNAs (circRNAs) in modulating neuroinflammation, immune responses, and cellular stress in Parkinson's disease (PD). CircRNAs function primarily as microRNA sponges, thereby regulating key signaling pathways involved in glial cell dysfunction and neuronal survival. Although functional evidence from cellular and animal models shows circRNAs can attenuate neuroinflammation, further in vivo validation and clinical evaluation in patient samples are needed.
key_finding_ja: circRNAはmicroRNAのスポンジとして機能し、パーキンソン病モデルにおいて神経炎症や神経細胞障害を制御することが明らかとなった。
why_it_matters_ja: circRNAを介した神経炎症の調節機構の解明は、パーキンソン病に対する新たな診断バイオマーカーや治療戦略の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: The role of PANoptosis regulatory networks in acute neurological injury.
abstract: Secondary injury following acute neurological insults-including stroke, spinal cord injury(SCI), traumatic brain injury(TBI), and subarachnoid hemorrhage(SAH)-is a major contributor to neuronal death and neuroinflammation; however, the complex molecular mechanisms driving these pathological processes remain poorly understood. The limited efficacy of traditional apoptosis-targeted therapies highlights the need to investigate alternative regulated cell death pathways governed by diverse and intricate regulatory networks. PANoptosis, an emerging form of inflammatory programmed cell death initially proposed to describe the crosstalk among apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis, is regulated by dynamic molecular complexes, such as the PANoptosome, which orchestrate multiple cell death-associated pathways and contribute to neuronal loss and the amplification of inflammatory responses. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms of PANoptosis and its functional roles in acute neurological injury, with a particular emphasis on its pathological regulatory networks associated with ischemic stroke and spinal cord injury. Furthermore, we highlight emerging therapeutic strategies targeting PANoptosis. Recent evidence has identified key molecular mediators, including Z-DNA-binding Protein 1 (ZBP1), receptor-Interacting Protein Kinase 1 (RIPK1), and TGF-β-Activated Kinase 1 (TAK1), which regulate PANoptosome assembly and downstream effector pathways, highlighting their potential as promising therapeutic targets. Inhibition of PANoptosis has been shown to markedly alleviate blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and neurological deficits. Additionally, this review addresses the translational challenges and future research directions in targeting PANoptosis, providing a theoretical basis for the development of multi-targeted neuroprotective strategies. FACTS: PANoptosis integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis via PANoptosome associated signaling. ZBP1, RIPK1, and TAK1 are key regulators of PANoptosis in acute neurological injury models. Inhibition of PANoptosis attenuates BBB disruption and improves functional recovery. OPEN QUESTIONS: How do PANoptosome subtypes differ among CNS cell types? Can PANoptosis-specific biomarkers be validated for clinical use? What are the optimal multi-target strategies for inhibiting PANoptosis without compromising immunity?
authors: Gao Z, Wang C, Yang W, Deng Z, Cao Y, Wang M, Wu Y, Shi S, Wang L, Kang H.
screening_reason: Reviews PANoptosis regulatory networks driving cell death and neuroinflammation in acute neurological injuries.
summary_ja: 急性神経傷害における制御された細胞死プログラムであるPANoptosisの分子メカニズムと役割に関するレビューである。PANoptosisはアポトーシス、ピロトーシス、ネクロトーシスが相互作用する炎症性細胞死であり、PANoptosomeによって調節される。ZBP1、RIPK1、TAK1などの分子がPANoptosomeの形成や下流シグナルを規制する主要な因子として特定されている。PANoptosisの抑制は血液脳関門の破綻や神経機能障害を軽減することが示されている。
summary_en: This review summarizes the regulatory networks and functional roles of PANoptosis in acute neurological injuries such as ischemic stroke and spinal cord injury. Key molecular mediators, including ZBP1, RIPK1, and TAK1, orchestrate PANoptosome assembly and drive neuroinflammation and neuronal death. Inhibiting PANoptosis has been shown to attenuate blood-brain barrier disruption and improve functional recovery in acute injury models.
key_finding_ja: ZBP1やRIPK1、TAK1によって調節されるPANoptosisの抑制が、急性神経傷害モデルにおいて血液脳関門の保護や機能回復をもたらすことが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: PANoptosisを標的とした治療戦略は、急性神経傷害後の神経炎症や組織損傷を低減させる新たな選択肢となる可能性がある。

title: RanBP2 promotes ferroptosis resistance and compromises therapeutic response by stabilizing SLC7A1 through LRSAM1 SUMOylation and ubiquitination in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: SUMOylation is characterized as a ubiquitin-like post-translational modification that exhibits mechanistic similarities with ubiquitination. Importantly, it modulates the ubiquitination levels of some target proteins, thereby influencing protein stability. Dysregulation of this modification pathway plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis and progression of various tumors. While recent studies have demonstrated that protein SUMOylation regulates tumor progression, the specific function and mechanism of Ran-binding protein 2 (RanBP2), an E3 SUMO ligase, remain to be elucidated in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). This study demonstrates that RanBP2 exhibits elevated expression in LUAD and correlates with poor prognosis. Functionally, RanBP2 inhibits ferroptosis and enhances the growth of LUAD cells. Mechanistically, RanBP2 augments the SUMOylation of E3 ubiquitin ligase leucine-rich repeat and sterile alpha motif-containing protein 1 (LRSAM1), facilitating its subsequent degradation in the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby reducing SLC7A11 degradation. The stabilized SLC7A11 protein suppresses ferroptosis and promotes LUAD cell growth. The identified RanBP2 inhibitor, amodiaquine (AQ), in combination with ferroptosis inducer sulfasalazine (SAS), effectively triggered ferroptosis and suppressed LUAD cell growth in vitro and in vivo. This combination enhanced T-cell infiltration and improved anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy. The research identifies a novel RanBP2-LRSAM1-SLC7A11 axis that promotes ferroptosis resistance and LUAD progression. The combination of AQ and SAS represents a promising therapeutic strategy for LUAD.
authors: Guo S, Zeng Y, Zhang Q, Zhao X, Jin H, Li B, Shen M, Yang Q, Yang L.
screening_reason: Provides a mechanistic study of protein post-translational modifications, specifically SUMOylation and ubiquitination governing LRSAM1 and SLC7A11 stability.
summary_ja: 肺腺がん（LUAD）におけるE3 SUMOリガーゼRanBP2の役割および機序を検討した。RanBP2はLUADで過剰発現しており予後不良と相関し、フェロトーシスを抑制してがん細胞の増殖を促進することが示された。分子機序として、RanBP2はE3ユビキチンリガーゼLRSAM1のSUMO化を亢進させて分解を促進し、これによりSLC7A11の分解を免れさせてフェロトーシス抵抗性を誘発する。RanBP2阻害剤とフェロトーシス誘導剤の併用は腫瘍増殖を抑制し免疫療法の効果を向上させた。
summary_en: This study identified the role of the E3 SUMO ligase RanBP2 in driving ferroptosis resistance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). RanBP2 enhances the SUMOylation and proteasomal degradation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase LRSAM1, which stabilizes SLC7A11 and inhibits ferroptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of RanBP2 combined with a ferroptosis inducer effectively triggered cell death, inhibited tumor growth, and enhanced anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy in LUAD models.
key_finding_ja: RanBP2はLRSAM1のSUMO化と分解を介してSLC7A11を安定化させ、肺腺がんにおけるフェロトーシス抵抗性と腫瘍伸長を促進する。
why_it_matters_ja: RanBP2を標的とした治療戦略は、フェロトーシス誘導や免疫療法に対する抵抗性を克服する新たな手段となる可能性がある。

title: Mitochondria-enriched BMSC exosomes restore microglia-neuron cross-talk in Parkinson's disease via PINK1/parkin and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways.
abstract: Background Mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation drive dopaminergic neuron loss in Parkinson's disease (PD). While BMSC-derived small extracellular vesicles (BMSC-Exo) are neuroprotective, their ability to repair mitochondrial deficits is limited. We engineered mitochondrial-enriched sEVs (Exo-Mito) to evaluate their effects on microglia-neuron interactions in a PD-relevant model. Methods BMSC-Exo-Mito were characterized via TEM, NTA, and immunoblotting. Their therapeutic efficacy was assessed using an MPP + -induced BV2/SH-SY5Y transwell co-culture model. Assessments included ROS levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP quantification, mitophagy flux, and signaling pathway analysis. Results Exo-Mito significantly restored mitochondrial homeostasis by reducing ROS, preserving membrane potential, and increasing ATP production. Mechanistically, Exo-Mito enhanced PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy and PGC-1alpha/TFAM-mediated biogenesis. In BV2 microglia, Exo-Mito suppressed the NF-kappaB/NLRP3 axis, reduced proinflammatory cytokines, and promoted M2 polarization. In SH-SY5Y cells with dopaminergic phenotype, Exo-Mito was associated with reactivated PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling, preserved tyrosine hydroxylase expression, and inhibited apoptosis. Functionally, Exo-Mito improved SH-SY5Y cell and restored microglial migratory capacity, showing superior efficacy to unmodified BMSC-Exo. Conclusion Mitochondria-enriched BMSC sEVs protect SH-SY5Y cells by coordinating mitochondrial quality control and modulating neuroinflammation. These findings support Exo-Mito as a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy for Parkinson's disease.
authors: Shi S, Liu R, Liu C, Chen Y, Pan Y, Wang C.
screening_reason: Focuses on restoring microglia-neuron cross-talk and inhibiting neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease models.
summary_ja: パーキンソン病（PD）モデルにおけるミトコンドリア濃縮骨髄由来幹細胞小細胞外小胞（Exo-Mito）の治療効果をMPP+誘発BV2/SH-SY5Y共培養系で評価した。Exo-MitoはROS減少やATP産生増大を通じてミトコンドリアの恒常性を回復させ、マイトファジーおよびミトコンドリア生合成を促進した。さらに、BV2ミクログリアの抗炎症化を誘導し、SH-SY5Y細胞のPI3K/Akt/mTOR経路を再活性化してアポトーシスを抑制した。
summary_en: Engineered mitochondria-enriched BMSC extracellular vesicles (Exo-Mito) were evaluated in an MPP+-induced BV2/SH-SY5Y co-culture model of Parkinson's disease. Exo-Mito restored mitochondrial homeostasis by reducing ROS and enhancing PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and mitochondrial biogenesis. In addition, Exo-Mito suppressed microglial inflammatory responses, promoted M2 polarization, and rescued dopaminergic SH-SY5Y cells through reactivation of PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling.
key_finding_ja: ミトコンドリア濃縮BMSC小外小胞は、ミトコンドリア品質管理の調節と神経炎症の抑制を通じてミクログリアと神経細胞間の相互作用を修復しドパミン作動性細胞を保護する。
why_it_matters_ja: 無細胞治療法としてのExo-Mitoは、ミトコンドリア障害と神経炎症が関与するパーキンソン病の新しい治療アプローチとなる可能性がある。

title: Liquiritigenin attenuates high-salt diet-induced neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cognitive impairment via NF-κB pathway inhibition.
abstract: Liquiritigenin (LG), a flavonoid compound extracted from licorice, possesses diverse pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. A high-salt diet (HSD) is a common dietary risk factor associated not only with hypertension but also with central nervous system injury. However, the underlying mechanisms and potential therapeutic interventions remain insufficiently explored. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective effects of LG against HSD-induced brain pathology and cognitive impairment in mice. The mechanism of action was further examined using NaCl-treated HT22 cells with LG intervention. By establishing HSD-related mouse and cellular models, administering different doses of LG, and performing neurobehavioral assessments, we evaluated its effects on brain tissue structure, cognitive performance, neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial function. The results demonstrated that in HSD-fed mice, LG attenuated hippocampal neuronal atrophy and death, thereby improving brain tissue morphology. Behavioral testing further revealed that LG enhanced motor performance and exploratory behavior, alleviating cognitive deficits. At the molecular level, LG reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory mediators while upregulating anti-inflammatory cytokines, effectively suppressing neuroinflammation. In addition, LG decreased cytoplasmic expression of mitochondrial DNA-related genes (d-loop, cox1, non-numt), increased ATP production, and improved mitochondrial function. Mechanistic studies further indicated that LG inhibits HSD-induced nuclear factor kappa-B p65 phosphorylation, reducing neuroinflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas NF-κB p65 overexpression abrogated these protective effects. In summary, LG protects against neuroinflammation and mitochondrial impairment by suppressing NF-κB signaling, thereby mitigating neurological dysfunction. These findings suggest that LG holds promise as a potential therapeutic agent for the prevention and treatment of HSD-related neurological disorders.
authors: Liu Y, Xu D, Shi Y, Li X, Li M, Zhang J, Yu X, Peng W, Chen H, Guan X, Dong J.
screening_reason: Evaluates the mechanisms by which liquiritigenin suppresses high-salt diet-induced neuroinflammation and NF-kappaB signaling.
summary_ja: 高塩分食（HSD）誘発性の脳病変および認知機能障害に対するリコリチゲニン（LG）の保護効果と作用機序をマウスおよびHT22細胞を用いて検討した。LG投与は海馬神経細胞の萎縮および死を抑制し、行動テストにおける認知機能や運動能力の低下を改善した。さらに、プロ炎症性因子の発現を抑え、ミトコンドリア機能を向上させるとともに、NF-κB p65のリン酸化を阻害することを示した。
summary_en: This study evaluated the protective effects of liquiritigenin (LG) in high-salt diet (HSD)-induced mouse and cell models of neurological impairment. LG treatment attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage, improved motor and cognitive behaviors, and reduced neuroinflammation. Furthermore, LG restored mitochondrial function and suppressed the NF-κB p65 pathway, counteracting HSD-induced central nervous system injury.
key_finding_ja: リコリチゲニンはNF-κBシグナル伝達を抑制することにより、高塩分食に起因する神経炎症とミトコンドリア障害を軽減し、認知機能を改善する。
why_it_matters_ja: 高塩分食に伴う脳機能障害の予防や治療において、リコリチゲニンが新たな治療薬候補となる可能性が期待される。

title: Fasudil Attenuates Fluoride-induced Neuronal Synaptic Damage by Inhibiting Microglial Inflammation.
abstract: Exposure to high levels of fluoride in drinking water has been linked to cognitive impairment, but the molecular mechanisms underlying this neurotoxicity are not fully understood. In this study, a subchronic rat model was used to investigate whether fluoride-induced synaptic damage involves RhoA/ROCK pathway-mediated microglial activation and inflammation. The role of fasudil, a specific RhoA/ROCK inhibitor, was also evaluated. The results demonstrated that fluoride activated the RhoA/ROCK cascade, stimulated microglial activation and subsequent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and resulted in hippocampal synaptic injury. Conversely, fasudil attenuated these effects by downregulating Iba1, TNF-α, and ROCK2 expression. Taken together, these findings establish that RhoA/ROCK signaling critically mediates fluoride-induced neuroinflammation and synaptic damage, thereby offering a mechanistic basis for assessing the neurotoxic risk of environmental fluoride exposure.
authors: Yang W, Bu K, Ren X, Qin S, Wang S, Chu F, Lu C, Liu Z, Liu J, Zhang Y, Yang X, Gao Y, Sun D, Sun H.
screening_reason: The research directly examines fasudil inhibition of microglial activation and RhoA/ROCK-mediated neuroinflammation in a fluoride toxicity model.
summary_ja: 本研究は、高濃度フッ素曝露による海馬シナプス損傷におけるRhoA/ROCK経路とミクログリア炎症の関与、および阻害剤ファスジルの効果をラットモデルで検証した。フッ素曝露はRhoA/ROCKシグナルを活性化し、ミクログリアの活性化と炎症性サイトカインの放出を引き起こしてシナプス障害を誘導した。一方、選択的RhoA/ROCK阻害剤であるファスジルは、Iba1、TNF-α、ROCK2の発現を低下させることでこれらの有害作用を軽減した。これらの結果は、RhoA/ROCK経路がフッ素誘発性神経炎症とシナプス損傷を制御することを示している。
summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of fasudil, a RhoA/ROCK inhibitor, on fluoride-induced synaptic damage and microglial inflammation in a subchronic rat model. Fluoride exposure activated the RhoA/ROCK pathway, prompting microglial activation and cytokine release that led to hippocampal synaptic injury. Fasudil administration attenuated these inflammatory and synaptic damages by downregulating Iba1, TNF-alpha, and ROCK2 expression.
key_finding_ja: RhoA/ROCK阻害剤ファスジルは、ミクログリアの活性化と炎症を抑制することでフッ素誘発性の海馬シナプス損傷を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: フッ素神経毒性のシグナル伝達機構が明示されたことで、環境化学物質による神経影響の評価や保護戦略の検討に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated immune regulation in central nervous system diseases: Mechanistic insights and exercise interventions.
abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) diseases are major contributors to long-term disability and cognitive impairment, with neuroinflammation and immune dysregulation closely implicated in their pathogenesis. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are phospholipid bilayer-enclosed membrane vesicles secreted by diverse cell types that mediate communication between the periphery and CNS through the delivery of various bioactive molecules, including proteins, lipids, and non-coding RNA, thereby exerting immunomodulatory functions. Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that EVs contribute to immune regulation during the initiation and progression of CNS diseases by modulating pathological processes, including neuroinflammation, pro-inflammatory polarization of glial cells, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and pyroptosis. Previous studies have reported that exercise exerts neuroprotective effects in CNS diseases through EVs-mediated immune regulation. This review summarizes and critically evaluates the biological characteristics of EVs, EV-mediated immunoregulatory mechanisms, the roles of EV-mediated immunoregulation in CNS diseases, and exercise interventions, thereby providing theoretical insights into the beneficial effects of exercise on brain health.
authors: Tang S, Lin Q, Tang Y, Geng Y.
screening_reason: The paper focuses directly on extracellular vesicle-mediated immune regulation and neuroinflammation in central nervous system diseases.
summary_ja: 本論文は、中枢神経系（CNS）疾患における細胞外小胞（EV）を介した免疫調節機構と運動介入の役割に関する総説である。EVはタンパク質や非翻訳RNAなどの生体分子を輸送し、神経炎症やグリア細胞のプロ炎症性分化、NLRP3インフラマソーム活性化、ピロトーシスを制御する。さらに、運動がEVの免疫調節作用を通じて神経保護効果を発揮することが実験研究で報告されている。本総説はEVの生物学的特性とCNS疾患での役割を整理し、脳の健康維持に向けた運動介入の論理的根拠を提示している。
summary_en: This review outlines the mechanisms by which extracellular vesicles (EVs) regulate neuroinflammation and immune responses in central nervous system diseases. EVs deliver bioactive molecules that modulate glial polarization, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and pyroptosis. Additionally, the review summarizes evidence that exercise exerts neuroprotective effects through EV-mediated immunomodulation.
key_finding_ja: 細胞外小胞（EV）は神経炎症やグリア細胞の免疫応答を仲介し、運動介入による神経保護作用の担い手となることが整理された。
why_it_matters_ja: EVを介した神経免疫調節の理解は、CNS疾患における脳保護メカニズムの解明および運動療法の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: In-Vitro Evaluation of HIV/SARS-CoV-2 Co-Infection Mediated Proteomic Changes in Astrocytes and Pericytes Reveals Altered Signaling Pathways Associated With Neurodegenerative Disorders.
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) survivors frequently experience a wide range of symptoms known as post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) or long COVID. Importantly, complications arising from microvascular dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and chronic neuroinflammation have been implicated in driving PASC within the central nervous system (CNS), known as neuro-PASC. Notably, people with HIV (PWH), who suffer from chronic neuroinflammation, BBB impairment, and glial cell dysfunction, collectively known as neuro-HIV, are generally at higher risk of neuro-PASC. The overlap between neuro-PASC and neuro-HIV raises concerns that HIV and SARS-CoV-2 co-infection may exacerbate neurological dysfunctions among PWH. In this study, using an in-vitro cell culture model, we examine the effects of HIV and SARS-CoV-2 mono- and co-infection in microglia, astrocytes, and pericytes. Our results demonstrated that majority of brain cell types support SARS-CoV-2 replication, in the presence and absence of HIV infection. Furthermore, in both mono- and co-infected cells, there were varying degree of up- and downregulation of SARS-CoV-2 host cell entry factors, such as ACE2, TMPRSS2, NRP1, and TRIM28, and inflammatory cytokines including IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β. Moreover, conditioned media collected from HIV, SARS-CoV-2, and HIV/SARS-CoV-2 co-infected astrocytes and pericytes were shown to be neurotoxic. Additionally, proteomic analysis has revealed a unique set of proteins significantly up/down regulated in HIV/SARS-CoV-2 co-infected astrocytes and pericytes. The gene set enrichment analysis of these proteins indicates dysregulation of lipid, energy, and immune metabolism pathways linked to neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These in-vitro findings indicate that astrocytes and pericytes from HIV/SARS-CoV-2 co-infection exhibit altered protein expression profiles, implicating dysregulated signaling pathways associated with neurodegenerative dysfunction.
authors: Acharya A, Thurman M, Sutar D, Olasunkanmi OI, Malik JR, Dyavar SR, Végvári Á, Byrareddy SN.
screening_reason: Examines glial neuroinflammation, cytokine expression, and neuroimmune signaling in HIV and SARS-CoV-2 CNS co-infection.
summary_ja: HIVおよびSARS-CoV-2の単独感染および共感染がミクログリア、アストロサイト、ペリサイトに与える影響をin vitroモデルで検証した。脳細胞の多くは感染の有無に関わらずウイルス複製を支持し、エントリー因子や炎症性サイトカインの発現変化が確認された。感染したアストロサイトおよびペリサイトからの条件培地は神経毒性を示した。プロテオミクス解析では、脂質・エネルギー・免疫代謝経路の異常が示され、神経変性疾患に関連するシグナル伝達の変化が明らかになった。
summary_en: This in vitro study investigated the impact of HIV and SARS-CoV-2 mono- and co-infection on microglia, astrocytes, and pericytes. Both mono- and co-infections altered the expression of host entry factors and inflammatory cytokines, and conditioned media from infected astrocytes and pericytes exhibited neurotoxicity. Proteomic analysis revealed significant dysregulation of lipid, energy, and immune metabolic pathways associated with neurodegenerative disorders.
key_finding_ja: HIVとSARS-CoV-2の共感染はアストロサイトやペリサイトのタンパク質発現を変化させ、神経変性疾患に関連するシグナル伝達経路の障害を引き起こす。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究はin vitroモデルに基づくものであり、ヒト体内におけるHIVとSARS-CoV-2の共感染が神経変性やNeuro-PASCの発症リスクを高める可能性を示唆している。

title: Barbaloin Attenuates Cisplatin-Induced Hippocampal Neurotoxicity by Suppressing Oxidative Stress, Neuroinflammation, and Apoptosis: In Vivo and In Silico Evidence.
abstract: The neurotoxicity of cisplatin (CIS) in the hippocampal leads to cognitive effects caused by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, apoptosis, and dysfunction of neurotransmitters. The major bioactive phytonutrient in Aloe vera is barbaloin (BLN), which has been shown to have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, but its neuroprotective ability against CIS-induced neurotoxicity has not been investigated. To assess the neuroprotective action of BLN in CIS-induced hippocampal neurotoxicity in rats and to understand the molecular interactions between BLN and major neuroinflammatory and apoptotic proteins. A total of 24 male Wistar rats were split into 4 groups (n = 6): control, CIS (5 mg/kg), CIS + BLN 25 mg/kg, and CIS + BLN 50 mg/kg over 21 days. Cognitive ability (Morris water maze), oxidative stress indicators (MDA, GSH, SOD, CAT), neuroinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, NF-κB, TGF-β1), caspase-3, neurotransmitters, and hippocampal histopathology were measured. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) with MM-GBSA analysis were done with TNF-α, TGF-β1, NF-κBp65, and caspase-3. BLN significantly reduced cognitive impairment, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis, and restored neurotransmitter homeostasis and hippocampal cytoarchitecture (all p bind = -56.07 kcal/mol for TGF-β1). BLN exhibits considerable neuroprotective properties against CIS-induced neurotoxicity in the hippocampus, suggesting its potential as a natural dietary phytonutrient supplement to ameliorate chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment.
authors: Syed RU, Akasha R, Elafandy NM, Abobaker SH, Al-Shammari AN, Altwalah LA, Aldafeeri RMM, Alfaki AIMA, Khan MSA, Ahmed AA.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
screening_reason: The study directly measures and demonstrates the suppression of neuroinflammatory cytokines and neurotoxicity in the hippocampus by barbaloin.
summary_ja: 本研究は、抗がん剤シスプラチン（CIS）によって誘導される海馬の神経毒性に対し、アロエベラに含まれるバルバロイン（BLN）の保護効果をラットモデルおよびイン・シリコ解析で検証した。CISを投与したラットにおいて、BLNの投与は認知機能障害、酸化ストレス、神経炎症、アポトーシスを有意に抑制した。さらに、BLNは海馬の組織構造と神経伝達物質の恒常性を回復させた。分子ドッキングおよび分子動力学シミュレーションにおいても、BLNはTNF-αやTGF-β1などの主要な炎症・アポトーシス関連タンパク質と強い結合親和性を示した。
summary_en: This study investigated the protective effects of barbaloin (BLN) against cisplatin-induced hippocampal neurotoxicity using rat models and in silico simulations. BLN administration significantly ameliorated cognitive impairment, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis in cisplatin-treated rats while restoring neurotransmitter levels. Computational docking and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed strong binding interactions between BLN and key neuroinflammatory and apoptotic proteins.
key_finding_ja: バルバロインは酸化ストレス、神経炎症、アポトーシスを抑制することにより、シスプラチン誘発性の海馬神経毒性および認知機能障害を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 化学療法に伴う認知機能障害（ケモブレイン）を軽減するサプリメントや補助療法としてバルバロインの有効性が示唆されるが、臨床応用にはヒトでの安全性と有効性の検証が必要である。

title: Age-Associated B Cells: Origins, Regulation, and Tissue-Specific Pathogenic Contributions in Autoimmune, Metabolic, and Neurological Diseases.
abstract: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) are a distinct B cell population characterized by coexpression of T-bet and CD11c. First described in aged female mice and autoimmune-prone strains, ABCs are now recognized to be associated with multiple human autoimmune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and multiple sclerosis, where their frequency correlates with disease activity. Their differentiation requires toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling, IFN-γ, IL-21, BCR engagement, with ZEB2 emerging as the nonredundant transcriptional master regulator of ABC identity. Here we review requirements for ABC differentiation, their defining phenotypic and functional features, and their tissue-specific distribution and pathogenic contributions in diverse inflammatory settings. A central theme is that ABCs are tissue-homing cells whose contribution extends beyond blood and lymphoid organs. In kidney, inflamed synovium, salivary glands, and adipose tissue, ABCs drive pathology through locally differentiated autoantibody-secreting cells, stromal activation, antigen presentation, and cytokine production. We further discuss roles for ABCs in neurological diseases, including their enrichment in the cerebrospinal fluid in multiple sclerosis (MS) and their contribution to neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease, and highlight the EBV-ABC axis as a mechanism linking viral infection to autoimmunity. In summary, ABCs are multi-functional, tissue-adaptable pathogenic effectors whose contributions to human disease extend beyond classical autoimmunity into metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration.
authors: Rubtsova K.
screening_reason: The review focuses on age-associated B cells and their contribution to neuroinflammation and neuroimmune interactions in CNS diseases.
summary_ja: 本総説は、T-betおよびCD11cを共発現する加齢関連B細胞（ABC）の分化機構と各種疾患での病理学的役割をまとめている。ABCの分化にはTLRシグナルやサイトカイン刺激、マスター転写因子ZEB2が必須であり、全身性エリテマトーデスや多発性硬化症などの自己免疫疾患で頻度が増加する。ABCは血中だけでなく腎臓、滑膜、中枢神経系などの組織へ浸潤し、自己抗体産生やサイトカイン放出を通じて局所炎症を引き起こす。さらに、多発性硬化症の髄液中での集積やアルツハイマー病における神経炎症への寄与についても論じられている。
summary_en: This review summarizes the origins, differentiation, and tissue-specific pathogenic roles of age-associated B cells (ABCs) expressing T-bet and CD11c. Beyond blood and lymphoid organs, ABCs migrate to target tissues including the central nervous system, contributing to neuroinflammation in multiple sclerosis and Alzheimer's disease. The authors highlight ABCs as multi-functional effectors that link viral infection, autoimmunity, and neurodegeneration.
key_finding_ja: 加齢関連B細胞（ABC）は組織特異的に浸潤し、自己免疫疾患のみならずアルツハイマー病などの神経変性疾患における神経炎症の増幅に寄与している。
why_it_matters_ja: ABCを標的とした治療アプローチは、難治性の自己免疫疾患や神経変性疾患に対する新たな治療戦略につながる可能性がある。

title: Carboxypeptidase E Alleviates Depressive-Like Behaviors in Mice by Regulating BDNF/Nrf2 Axis-Mediated Ferroptosis.
abstract: Carboxypeptidase E (CPE) may be a therapeutic target for depression. This study investigated the mechanistic insights into the possible regulatory role of CPE in ferroptosis in a mouse model of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced depression. One week before CUMS exposure, mice received injections of adeno-associated virus-CPE. One week after CUMS induction, the Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 was administered. Behavioral tests were performed 3 weeks after CUMS induction. Ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1-positive cells and inflammatory cytokine levels in the CA1 region were assessed by immunofluorescence and ELISA. Hippocampal pathological and neuronal damage were evaluated using H&E and Nissl staining. Additionally, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) signaling, ferroptosis markers, oxidative stress indices, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), and Fe2+ levels were measured using western blot, RT-qPCR, and biochemical assays. CPE overexpression alleviated CUMS-induced depression-like behaviors and hippocampal damage in mice. CPE overexpression reduced microglial activation, neuronal degeneration, and pro-inflammatory factors. It also attenuated oxidative stress by decreasing malondialdehyde, reactive oxygen species, and lactate dehydrogenase while elevating superoxide dismutase and glutathione-S-transferase activities. Mechanistically, CPE activated the BDNF/Nrf2 axis, increased GPX4 activity, suppressed acyl-CoA synthetase long chain family member 4 expression, and reduced iron accumulation. All protective effects of CPE overexpression were reversed by ML385. CPE overexpression activates the BDNF/Nrf2 signaling axis to inhibit ferroptosis, thereby reducing neuroinflammation and depression-like behaviors in mice. This work further clarifies the pathogenesis of depression, enriches pathophysiological theories, and provides key experimental evidence for early intervention and target development.
authors: Li W, Meng F, Li J, Lv L.
screening_reason: The principal findings center on reducing microglial activation and neuroinflammation in a depression model via the BDNF/Nrf2 axis.
summary_ja: 慢性予測不能軽度ストレス誘発うつ病マウスモデルを用いて、カルボキシペプチダーゼE（CPE）のフェロトーシスおよび神経炎症制御における役割を検討した。CPEの過剰発現は、うつ様行動および海馬の組織損傷を軽減し、ミクログリアの活性化や炎症性サイトカインの放出を抑制した。さらに、CPEはBDNF/Nrf2軸を活性化してGPX4活性を高め、鉄蓄積や酸化ストレス、フェロトーシスを抑制した。Nrf2阻害剤であるML385の投与により、CPE過剰発現によるこれらの保護効果は消失した。
summary_en: This study evaluated the regulatory mechanism of Carboxypeptidase E (CPE) in a mouse model of chronic unpredictable mild stress-induced depression. CPE overexpression attenuated depression-like behaviors, microglial activation, neuroinflammation, and hippocampal damage by suppressing ferroptosis and oxidative stress. Mechanistically, CPE activated the BDNF/Nrf2 axis, and its neuroprotective effects were reversed by an Nrf2 inhibitor.
key_finding_ja: カルボキシペプチダーゼEの過剰発現はBDNF/Nrf2軸の活性化を介してフェロトーシスと神経炎症を抑制し、マウスのうつ様行動を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: CPEとフェロトーシス制御機構の関連性が解明されたことで、うつ病の新たな治療標的の開発に貢献することが期待される。

title: Citrullination-associated transcriptional states identify a non-canonical invasive program in malignant epithelial cells and correlate with SPP1-CD44 immune microenvironment niches in thyroid cancer.
abstract: Background Citrullination, a post-translational modification catalyzed by protein arginine deiminases (PADIs), has been implicated in malignant progression across multiple cancer types. However, its cellular distribution, functional significance, and role in microenvironment remodeling in thyroid cancer remain largely unknown. Methods We integrated single-cell transcriptomics (GSE232237, 92,519 cells), spatial transcriptomics (GSE250521), and TCGA-THCA bulk transcriptomic data. Malignant epithelial cells were identified using CopyKAT. A PADI-family-based citrullination score (CitrScore) was calculated per cell. Functional states, regulon networks, co-expression modules, drug sensitivity, cell-cell communication, and in silico CD44 knockout were systematically analyzed. CD44 knockdown and overexpression experiments were performed in TPC-1 and 8505C cells. authors: Tian Z, Zhu P, Zhao X, Yang F.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates the functional impact and state alterations of citrullination, a specific protein post-translational modification.
summary_ja: 甲状腺がんにおけるタンパク質翻訳後修飾の一種であるシトルリン化の役割を、単一細胞・空間トランスクリプトミクス解析および細胞実験により解析した。シトルリン化スコア（CitrScore）は悪性上皮細胞に強く濃縮されており、上皮間葉転換や低酸素応答と相関していた。細胞間相互作用解析により、CitrScoreが高い細胞はSPP1陽性マクロファージとCD44シグナルを介して強く相互作用していることが示された。CD44のノックダウンおよび過剰発現実験により、CD44が悪性上皮細胞の浸潤性および遊走性を促進することが確認された。
summary_en: This study identified a citrullination-associated malignant state in thyroid cancer using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics along with in vitro cell experiments. High citrullination scores correlated with EMT, hypoxia responses, and crosstalk between malignant cells and SPP1-positive macrophages via the SPP1-CD44 axis. Functional validation in cell lines confirmed that CD44 promotes cell migration and invasion, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target.
key_finding_ja: 甲状腺がんにおいてシトルリン化関連転写状態が悪性上皮細胞の浸潤プログラムを形成し、SPP1-CD44軸を介したマクロファージとの相互作用に関与することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: シトルリン化と腫瘍微小環境の相互作用の解明は、甲状腺がんにおける新たな標的治療法の開発に役立つ可能性がある。
